name: XML Validator
description: Check whether XML documents are well-formed and point to the first syntax error
backend_requirements: Access control: anyone may check XML without saving; require auth for saving checks and for reading or deleting the check history; restrict each user's history to that user; admin endpoints are restricted to the admin account
A check decides whether the submitted text is a well-formed XML document (syntax only; there is no schema validation); xml is a required non-empty string of at most 200000 characters, otherwise 400

A check result always carries valid, error, line, column and root_element: a well-formed document has error, line and column null and root_element set to the name of its root element; otherwise error is a readable message for the first problem found, line and column are its 1-based position (null when unknown) and root_element is null
A document that is not well-formed is still a successful check: it answers 200 (or 201 when saved) with valid false
POST /api/validations checks the same way and saves the result to the signed-in user's history with xml_preview (the first 200 characters of the document)

GET /api/validations returns the signed-in user's active checks newest first; ?valid= (true or false) filters by result, ?page= and ?page_size= page the result (page_size default 20, at most 100), and total counts every matching check
DELETE /api/validations/:id removes one of the signed-in user's checks permanently
Deactivated checks (is_active false) are left out of the owner's history; the admin overview still lists them
Errors answer with a JSON object {"detail": "<message>"}: 400 for invalid input, 401 without a valid token, 403 for a non-admin on admin endpoints, 404 for unknown ids
frontend_requirements: Everyone can check XML; signed-in users also get a 'Save to history' switch and a history panel, and visitors see a 'Sign in to keep a history' prompt in their place
Sign-in and registration forms that call /api/auth/login and /api/auth/register; keep the token for later requests, show the signed-in username and offer sign-out
A large monospace text area with line numbers for the XML and a Validate button; with 'Save to history' on the check goes through /api/validations, otherwise through /api/validate/xml
Result display: a clear valid state naming the root element, or an invalid state with the error message and its line and column, and the offending line highlighted in the text area
A 'Load sample' button that fills in a short well-formed example document
History panel: the user's checks with result, preview and time, a valid/invalid filter, previous/next paging and a delete control per entry
admin_requirements: Admin overview: every saved check, active or not, with its user and total, active and inactive counts
Toggle a check's active status from the overview
